To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proxy process is not a sufficient means of addressing the concerns of shareholder activists.

(1) shareholder activism is an important force in the corporate world; (2) the most important shareholder activists are hedge funds; (3) shareholder activists and the companies they target engage in a complex dialogue; (4) this dialogue has a significant impact on the behavior of companies; and (5) this dialogue is a key element of the corporate governance system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of the relationship between shareholder activists and the corporations they target, and how that relationship is changing.
the question of what happens when the shareholder activist and the corporation meet.
the nature of the dialogue that takes place between shareholder activists (SA) and corporations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no clear evidence that the proxy voting process has been effective in addressing the issues of corporate social responsibility.
the current proxy vote system is not an adequate method of addressing corporate governance problems.
proxy voting is an important tool for the shareholders to express their opinion about the company’s management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are working to improve the relationship between shareholder activists and corporations.
the proxy voting system is a very important part of our work, but it is not the end goal.
the shareholder activism industry is a complex and nuanced space.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for a more robust dialogue between shareholder activists and corporations.
shareholder activists and corporations are not as far apart as they might think.
shareholder engagement is a two-way process.
